## Fatal findings

1. `cor-gaft-recovers-the-free-group-and-abelianisation-adjoints` — `[L2]`, Statement, and proof step 3.1

   [The item](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/cor-gaft-recovers-the-free-group-and-abelianisation-adjoints.md:36) restates `[L2]` as though supplied initial comma objects unconditionally assemble via the cited GAFT functor form. Step 3.1 then explicitly says the abelian-inclusion branch “needs no completeness or continuity hypothesis.”

   This changes the cited theorem’s hypotheses. The actual dependency states:

   > Let \(U:\mathcal A\to\mathcal C\), where \(\mathcal A\) is complete and locally small and \(U\) is continuous.

   See [the dependency Statement](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-general-adjoint-functor-theorem-functor-form.md:28). The proof never establishes completeness of \(\mathbf{Ab}\); moreover, its assertion that these hypotheses are unnecessary directly contradicts the cited Statement. `[L3]` independently supplies the already-known abelianisation adjunction, but that does not license the claim that this GAFT theorem applies.

   The contract also falsely marks the `one` boundary `not_applicable`, saying no singleton index occurs, although the Statement and step 3.1 explicitly use singleton solution sets.

   **Severity: fatal — inaccurate citation and unlicensed inference.**

2. `cex-a-complete-category-whose-coseparating-sets-are-never-small` — Counterexample and verification steps 1.1–1.2

   [The construction](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/cex-a-complete-category-whose-coseparating-sets-are-never-small.md:28) declares objects to be families indexed by every ordinal and morphisms to be coordinatewise functions. Under the library’s ZFC convention, ordinary functions are sets of ordered pairs; a function with domain the proper class of ordinals is instead only a particular definable class-function schema. The library expressly requires class-sized categorical data to expand to ordinary ZFC formulas and refuses categories whose objects are classes treated as members; see [the class convention](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/rem-category-theory-class-and-size-conventions.md:25) and [the category convention](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-category.md:27). This is also the standard foundational distinction discussed in [Shulman, *Set theory for category theory*](https://arxiv.org/abs/0810.1279).

   The item supplies neither set codes for its objects—such as a set support plus exceptional coordinate values—nor set codes for its coordinatewise morphisms. Step 1.1’s observation that a morphism is “determined” by set-many coordinates does not turn the stated proper-class family of coordinate maps into a set-valued morphism. Consequently, no category satisfying the repository’s convention has actually been defined, so the local-smallness and completeness conclusions do not follow.

   **Severity: fatal — missing size/class distinction in an AI-generated construction.**

## Nonfatal finding

3. `ex-the-subobject-poset-of-the-integers-in-abelian-groups` — proof-contract `iff-forward` and `iff-reverse` boundary rows

   Both rows claim the item is not proved by a biconditional. But [the Example](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/ex-the-subobject-poset-of-the-integers-in-abelian-groups.md:29) explicitly asserts
   \[
   [n\mathbb Z]\le[m\mathbb Z]\Longleftrightarrow m\mid n,
   \]
   and step 1.2 proves both directions. The proof is mathematically complete; only the boundary dispositions are false.

   **Severity: nonfatal.**

Coverage: I fully read all 22 assigned items, both containing page files, all 53 additional direct dependency files, all 89 cited contract clauses, and every assigned boundary worksheet. I sampled nothing and was unable to check nothing. I also tested the empty/zero objects, empty diagrams and families, \(n=0\) and \(n=1\), degenerate parameters, and applicable iff directions. No other fatal defect was found.
